title: Hedged warmstart causing TTFT surge — eviction-throttle emergency patch
creator: Liam Chen
description: Several enterprise customers from Hosted and Dedicated reported a sharp regression in Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) and overall tokens/sec for short chat calls after deploying runtime-1.19 (hedged priming feature). Symptoms: large 90th/95th percentile TTFT increases and sustained token throughput drops on multi-model fanout workloads. This ticket drives an emergency mitigations + short-term patch to contain impact and a follow-up investigation for a permanent fix.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send a mix of short chat and medium-length completions to a multiplexed model router across 3+ models.
2) Target bursts (~200 req/s) from a small set of clients to simulate regional surge.
3) Observe 1st-token latency distribution and tokens/sec on impacted workers over 5 minutes.
4) Reproduce on a staging cluster with hedged_warmstart feature flag enabled versus disabled.
observed_behavior: After deploying hedged priming (parallel warmstart of KV/cache during request admission), affected clusters showed repeated KV cache churn: prefetched contexts were evicted immediately by an aggressive LRU eviction when multiple hedged priming jobs race. Result: repeated cache misses, heavier kernel startup, microbatch handshake stalls and a 30-60% drop in tokens/sec for affected models; TTFT 90th jumped from ~110ms to 900-1,200ms.
root_cause_hypothesis: Combination of: (a) hedged warmstart creating transient working-set spikes, (b) eviction policy not bounding priming allocations, (c) microbatch handshake backpressure amplifying latency for short requests. Kernel/memory selection looked correct; issue is resource lifecycle and prioritization rather than kernel bug.
mitigation_plan:
Short-term emergency patch (runtime-1.19.1-hotfix):
- Introduce eviction_throttle window: tag priming allocations as grace->do-not-evict for X seconds.
- Limit concurrent hedged priming per worker to 1 extra priming job for high-priority short requests.
- Add backoff for prefetch when worker free memory < threshold.
- Expose hedged_warmstart feature flag (off by default) and fast rollback path to fully disable hedging.
- Add telemetry counters (hedge_attempts, hedged_evictions, prefetch_backoffs) and alert rule for >10% tokens/sec drop.
rollout_plan:
1) Cut runtime-1.19.1-hotfix image with feature flag and throttle knobs.
2) Canary deploy to two low-latency clusters (one hosted, one dedicated) for 30 minutes.
3) If canary stable, ramp to 20% of traffic across regions for 1 hour.
4) Full rollout in 3 hours if no regressions.
5) If regression persists, rollback by toggling hedged_warmstart=false and/or reverting image.
6) Postmortem and permanent fix design in follow-up ticket.
test_plan:
- Unit/Integration tests for eviction_throttle state transition.
- Load test in staging replicating mixed short/medium workload with synthetic clients.
- Canary monitors: TTFT p50/p90/p95, tokens/sec, hedged_evictions.
- Run e2e customer-sim scenario from Customer X’s workload snapshot (sanitized).
verification_criteria:
- p95 TTFT returns to <= 200ms on canary clusters.
- tokens/sec degradation <5% relative to baseline.
- hedged_evictions reduced by >90% compared to failing deployment.
- No increased memory OOMs after throttle applied.
implementation_notes:
- Patch implemented in hedging module with small API change: priming allocation includes 'grace_until' timestamp.
- Kept default throttle window conservative (3s) to avoid stale warm caches.
- Added a quick toggle in admin console for hedged_warmstart for emergency ops.
- Coordinated with Dedicated infra team for capacity knobs and with Customer Success on escalations.
rollback_plan:
1) Toggle hedged_warmstart=false from admin console (immediate effect).
2) If toggling fails to fully remediate, revert runtime image and redeploy previous stable (runtime-1.19.0).
3) Notify customers and schedule maintenance window if full revert required.
communication_plan:
- Sent initial incident update to impacted customers (PM: Rachel Gupta).
- Slack #oncall + #infra-alerts: pinned canary link and mitigation steps.
- External customer update draft available in Confluence for CS to send once canary verifies.
postmortem_actions: Refine eviction policy heuristics to consider priming tag
Add automated chaos tests for hedging under surge
